title: Newton's Second Law (F = ma)

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Laws of Motion

explanation: The net force acting on an object equals the product of its mass and the acceleration produced. This is the simplified form for constant mass; the more general form states that net force equals the rate of change of momentum, which also correctly handles situations where mass itself changes (e.g. a rocket burning fuel).

variables.meaning: Net external force acting on the object

conditions: F must be the NET force — the vector sum of all forces acting on the object, not any single applied force

workedExample.scenario: A net force of 20 N acts on a 4 kg object.

commonMistakes: Using only the applied force instead of the NET force (forgetting to subtract friction, gravity components, etc.).
Forgetting that F = ma assumes constant mass — variable-mass systems need the momentum form F = dp/dt instead.
genZNote: This formula looks innocent until the exam adds friction, an incline, or a pulley — always find the NET force first.
